subject: Bird Nest
fact: Many birds build nests to hold eggs and protect chicks.

subject: Eagle Nest
fact: Eagles build large nests of sticks called eyries.

subject: Hummingbird Nest
fact: Hummingbirds build tiny cup nests using plant fibers and spider silk.

subject: Weaver Bird Nest
fact: Weaver birds knot grass into hanging woven nests.

subject: Penguin Colony
fact: Many penguins raise chicks in large groups called colonies.

subject: Rabbit Burrow
fact: Rabbits dig underground burrows for shelter and raising young.

subject: Prairie Dog Town
fact: Prairie dogs live in connected underground burrow systems called towns.

subject: Fox Den
fact: Foxes use dens for resting and raising kits.

subject: Wolf Den
fact: Wolf pups are often born in sheltered dens.

subject: Bear Den
fact: Bears use dens for winter shelter and to raise newborn cubs.

subject: Badger Sett
fact: Badgers live in underground homes called setts.

subject: Meerkat Burrow
fact: Meerkats dig complex burrows with many entrances.

subject: Mole Tunnel
fact: Moles dig underground tunnels while searching for food.

subject: Groundhog Burrow
fact: Groundhogs build burrows with separate chambers.

subject: Ant Colony
fact: Ants build colonies with tunnels and chambers underground or in wood.

subject: Termite Mound
fact: Some termites build tall mounds that help control temperature inside.

subject: Bee Hive
fact: Honey bees live together in hives filled with wax comb.

subject: Wasp Nest
fact: Paper wasps build nests from chewed wood fibers.

subject: Spider Web
fact: Many spiders spin silk webs to catch food or protect eggs.

subject: Silkworm Cocoon
fact: Silkworm caterpillars spin silk cocoons before becoming moths.

subject: Butterfly Chrysalis
fact: Many butterflies transform inside a chrysalis.

subject: Snail Shell
fact: A snail carries a hard shell that protects its soft body.

subject: Hermit Crab Shell
fact: Hermit crabs move into empty shells for protection.

subject: Turtle Shell
fact: A turtle's shell is part of its skeleton.

subject: Armadillo Burrow
fact: Armadillos dig burrows to rest and escape heat.

subject: Beaver Lodge
fact: Beavers build lodges from sticks mud and vegetation.

subject: Muskrat Lodge
fact: Muskrats build dome-shaped lodges in wetlands.

subject: Otter Holt
fact: An otter's resting den can be called a holt.

subject: Platypus Burrow
fact: Platypuses dig riverbank burrows for resting and nesting.

subject: Crocodile Nest
fact: Crocodiles lay eggs in nests made of sand or vegetation.

subject: Alligator Nest
fact: Alligators build mound nests from plants and mud.

subject: Sea Turtle Nest
fact: Sea turtles bury their eggs in sandy beach nests.

subject: Frog Pond
fact: Many frogs lay eggs in ponds or other freshwater habitats.

subject: Salamander Log
fact: Many salamanders shelter under damp logs and rocks.

subject: Fish Reef
fact: Coral reefs provide hiding places and food for many fish.

subject: Clownfish Anemone
fact: Clownfish shelter among the tentacles of sea anemones.

subject: Octopus Den
fact: Octopuses hide in rocky dens and may decorate the entrance with shells.

subject: Moray Eel Crevice
fact: Moray eels often rest in narrow cracks in coral reefs.

subject: Lobster Crevice
fact: Lobsters shelter in rocky crevices during the day.

subject: Seahorse Seagrass
fact: Seahorses use their tails to grip seagrass and coral.

subject: Polar Bear Snow Den
fact: Pregnant polar bears dig snow dens where cubs are born.

subject: Arctic Fox Den
fact: Arctic fox families may reuse the same den for many years.

subject: Penguin Nest
fact: Many penguins nest on stones or sheltered ice-free ground rather than building nests from ice.

subject: Seal Ice Hole
fact: Some seals keep breathing holes open in sea ice.

subject: Walrus Haul-Out
fact: Walruses rest together on beaches or floating ice called haul-outs.

subject: Bat Cave
fact: Many bats roost in caves trees or buildings.

subject: Owl Tree Hollow
fact: Some owls nest in natural hollows inside trees.

subject: Squirrel Drey
fact: A squirrel's leafy tree nest is called a drey.

subject: Woodpecker Cavity
fact: Woodpeckers carve nest cavities into tree trunks.

subject: Raccoon Tree Den
fact: Raccoons often sleep in hollow trees or sheltered dens.

subject: Koala Eucalyptus Tree
fact: Koalas spend much of their lives resting and feeding in eucalyptus trees.

subject: Orangutan Tree Nest
fact: Orangutans build new sleeping nests from branches and leaves.

subject: Gorilla Ground Nest
fact: Gorillas make simple sleeping nests from leaves and branches.

subject: Chimpanzee Tree Nest
fact: Chimpanzees often build sleeping nests high in trees.

subject: Lion Pride Territory
fact: Lions rest in shaded grassland areas within their pride's territory.

subject: Elephant Water Hole
fact: Elephants travel to water holes to drink bathe and cool off.

subject: Giraffe Savanna
fact: Giraffes live in open savannas and woodlands where tall trees grow.

subject: Camel Desert Shelter
fact: Camels rest in desert shade and are adapted to hot dry habitats.

subject: Mountain Goat Cliff
fact: Mountain goats live on steep rocky slopes that help protect them from predators.

subject: Puffin Burrow
fact: Puffins often nest in burrows or rocky crevices near the sea.
